entries.title: Inside the race between Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos for control of outer space

entries.title: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries, officials say, after brief truce

entries.title: Greetings from Mexico City, where a bullfighting ban doesn't stop this matador training

entries.snippet: Gianni Infantino apologized to FIFA's ruling council on Thursday for "mistakes" in his secretive investment plan for the World Cup but didn't give details sought by his toughest critics who want to oust him as the president of soccer's governing body.

entries.title: Prince Harry and Meghan make first joint appearances since returning to UK
entries.snippet: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan appeared together in a trio of charity visits Thursday, their first joint public appearance since moving back to England, as they seek to rebuild their brand in Britain after walking away from royal duties six years ago.

entries.snippet: Romanian authorities launched search and rescue operations off the Black Sea coast Thursday after a drone struck a ship which then caught fire, the latest in a spate of strikes that has raised fears that Russia's war in Ukraine is spreading.

entries.snippet: President Trump will travel to Georgia on Friday to stump for Republican Senate candidate Mike Collins. Collins is in an uphill battle against incumbent Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff. Liz Landers visited Georgia for a closer look at that race.

entries.title: Frustrated with Trump, voters overwhelmingly want change, AP-NORC poll finds
entries.snippet: A strong majority of voters believe that President Donald Trump is falling short at home and abroad, and they want major change in the upcoming midterm elections, according to a new AP-NORC poll that raises serious warning signs for the Republican Party at a critical moment.

entries.title: Why small colleges are closing and the toll on students and communities
entries.snippet: Across the nation, scores of small private colleges and universities are either closing or under threat. As each school shutters, students, faculty, and the surrounding community struggle to find a way forward. Paul Solman reports on one such school and the effects of its demise.

entries.title: David Byrne explores the art of rediscovery in 'Sleeping Beauties'

entries.title: 3 students and a teacher killed in Oregon elementary school shooting, police say
entries.snippet: Three children ages 5, 8 and 11 and a teacher were killed in a Thursday shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, police said.

entries.title: Retail sales saw 0.8% bump in September, but big chunk of spending went to paying for gas
entries.snippet: Excluding business at gas stations, retail sales rose 0.2% in September. The government figures aren't adjusted for inflation, which accelerated last month as gasoline and many other goods and services became more expensive.

entries.title: Wisconsin elections officials issue guidance for handling federal agents at polls
entries.snippet: Elections officials in battleground Wisconsin on Thursday approved guidance for local clerks to help them know what to do if federal law enforcement officials show up at the polls on Election Day, as some activists fear might happen.

entries.snippet: Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson will meet on the debate stage Thursday in one of the nation's most closely watched races during this midterm election cycle.

entries.title: How much longer will consumers be willing to muscle through higher prices?

entries.title: Bus, train collide, injuring 19 at Channel Tunnel terminal
entries.snippet: A minibus carrying truck drivers collided with a freight train near the Channel Tunnel entrance in France, injuring 19 people, two of them severely. Authorities launched an inquiry into what caused the accident.

entries.title: Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro pleads not guilty to torture charges
entries.snippet: Maduro and his wife were charged with leading a state-sponsored repression campaign that tortured scores of victims during his presidency from 2013 to 2026.

entries.title: Self-replicating AI: Is your fridge a cybersecurity risk?
entries.snippet: Anthropic researchers warn that AI worms could soon target connected household devices and spread from one device to another. Cyberattacks on French supermarkets illustrate just how vulnerable such systems can be.

entries.title: Middle East updates: Houthis target Yemen government palace in Aden
entries.snippet: Houthi rebels say they targeted Saudi military assets in a rare attack on the interim seat of Yemen's internationally recognized government. Meanwhile, vessels are again under fire near the Strait of Hormuz. More on DW.

entries.title: Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
entries.snippet: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.

entries.title: Trump says execution of Fort Hood shooter will not be livestreamed
entries.snippet: Trump said the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan can be viewed in person by families of the victims if they wish. The decision comes after bipartisan backlash regarding the Pentagon's plans to livestream the execution.

entries.title: Russia arrests Swedish national, claims he's Ukraine fighter
entries.snippet: Russian intelligence agents have arrested a Swedish man they say led a Ukrainian drone unit. He was detained at Russia's western border and is accused of planning acts of terrorism and sabotage.

entries.title: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian refineries as Zelenskyy says 'we're done'
entries.snippet: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Ukraine will again attack Russian energy sites, as Moscow has ignored a claim by US President Trump that an "energy ceasefire" had been agreed. Russia reported two attacks on refineries.

entries.title: Can Kenya preserve the democratic space Raila Odinga fought for?
entries.snippet: One year after the former prime minister's death, Kenyans are reflecting on his contribution to democracy and national reconciliation. Odinga's "handshakes" with his political rivals remain the subject of much debate.

entries.title: EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
entries.snippet: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.

entries.title: Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing
entries.snippet: Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

entries.title: Resignation of Bärbel Bas shines light on harsh era of German politics
entries.snippet: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas has stepped down, citing her need to grieve a loved one and leave behind the harsh realities of government. So how did German politics get so heated?

entries.title: Hamburg court jails 2 men over plot to attack Jewish leaders on behalf of Iran
entries.snippet: The men were found guilty of espionage and attempted murder. According to the court, they planned to attack the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany and president of the German-Israeli society.

entries.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
entries.snippet: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

entries.title: Starlink: How Elon Musk's company influences geopolitics
entries.snippet: Designed to bring internet access to remote regions, Elon Musk's Starlink has become vital in crisis regions and war zones. But Ukraine also shows the risks of depending on the service.

entries.title: Hypersonic missiles highlight arms race on Korean Peninsula
entries.snippet: Both South and North Korea have tested weapons feared by military planners for their speed and ability to maneuver in flight.

entries.title: Thousands of German gamblers could sue for their money back
entries.snippet: German gamblers may finally be able to beat the house, thanks to new court rulings in the EU and in Germany. The decisions could help gambling addicts — but the legal road might be difficult.

entries.title: School roof collapse in Pakistan's Peshawar kills dozens of students and one teacher
entries.snippet: Local authorities said more than 50 other people were injured in the disaster. Roof collapses have become increasingly common in Pakistan.

entries.title: Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
entries.snippet: Consuming alcohol is no longer permitted at train stations in Germany, to improve the lot of travelers and staff alike. Coalition talks are restarting in Berlin, and an inmate is loose in Essen.
